variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
(define x 10)
(define y 20)

;; Local variables (Racket typically uses [] for let)
(let ([a 1]
      [b 2])
  (+ a b))

(let* ([a 1]
       [b (+ a 1)])
  b)
variables.notes: define is used for module-level variables. let and let* create local lexical scopes. Racket idiomatically uses square brackets for binding pairs.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
42                   ; integer
3.14                 ; flonum
3/4                  ; exact rational
3+4i                 ; complex
"Hello"              ; string
#\A                  ; character
'symbol              ; symbol
'(1 2 3)             ; list
#(1 2 3)             ; vector
#t                   ; boolean true
#f                   ; boolean false
data_types.notes: Racket inherits Scheme's rich numeric tower and fundamental data types, adding structures, hash tables, and byte strings as core concepts.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
(+ 1 2 3)    ; => 6
(- 10 4)     ; => 6
(* 2 3)      ; => 6
(/ 10 2)     ; => 5

(= 1 1)      ; Numeric equality
(equal? "a" "a") ; Deep structural equality
(eqv? 'a 'a) ; Value equality
(eq? 'a 'a)  ; Pointer equality

(and #t #f)  ; => #f
(or #f #t)   ; => #t
(not #t)     ; => #f
operators.notes: Functions are used in prefix notation. equal? is the most general equality predicate.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: if is for two-branch logic, cond for multi-branch. when and unless are used when you have side effects and no else branch is needed.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
;; Racket's powerful comprehension comprehensions
(for ([i (in-range 10)])
  (displayln i))

(for ([x '(a b c)]
      [y '(1 2 3)])
  (printf "~a: ~a\n" x y))

;; Accumulating results
(for/list ([i (in-range 5)])
  (* i i)) ; => '(0 1 4 9 16)
for_loop.notes: Racket has a comprehensive set of for macros (for, for/list, for/fold, etc.) that replace traditional loop structures with sequence abstractions.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
;; Using named let
(let loop ([x 0])
  (when (< x 10)
    (displayln x)
    (loop (add1 x))))

;; Iterating indefinitely until a condition
(let loop ()
  (let ([v (read-line)])
    (unless (eof-object? v)
      (displayln v)
      (loop))))
while_loop.notes: While Racket has imperative constructs, tail-recursive named let is the standard way to express stateful iteration.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
(define (add a b)
  (+ a b))

;; Lambda
(define multiply (lambda (x y) (* x y)))

;; Keyword arguments
(define (greet name #:greeting [g "Hello"])
  (string-append g ", " name))

(greet "Alice" #:greeting "Hi")
functions.notes: Functions support optional, keyword, and rest arguments. Racket provides a rich contract system (define/contract) for type-like checking.

arrays.title: Arrays (Vectors)
arrays.code:
;; Vectors
(make-vector 5 0)
#(1 2 3 4 5) ; Literal immutable vector

(define v (vector 1 2 3))
(vector-ref v 0)
(vector-set! v 0 42)

;; Iterating over a vector
(for ([val (in-vector v)])
  (displayln val))
arrays.notes: Vectors are fixed-size, contiguous memory structures. Sequences work natively with vectors via in-vector.

maps.title: Maps (Hash Tables)
maps.code:
;; Mutable hash table
(define ht (make-hash))
(hash-set! ht 'key "value")
(hash-ref ht 'key)

;; Immutable hash table
(define ht2 (hash 'a 1 'b 2))
(define ht3 (hash-set ht2 'c 3))

;; Hash table iteration
(for ([(k v) (in-hash ht2)])
  (printf "~a = ~a\n" k v))
maps.notes: Racket provides both mutable (make-hash) and immutable (hash) hash tables. Immutable hashes share structure for efficiency.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: with-handlers intercepts exceptions based on predicates (like exn:fail?). Exceptions in Racket are typically structs inheriting from exn.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
;; Single-line comment in Lisp
#|
 Multi-line block comment
|#
(defun add (a b)
  "Documentation string for function"
  (+ a b))
comments.notes: Racket uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.code:
(def x 42)          ; Integer
(def pi 3.14159)    ; Float
(def ratio 1/3)     ; Exact rational ratio
(def hex #xFF)      ; Hexadecimal
numbers.notes: Racket supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.notes: Racket treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Racket performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.code:
(def s "Hello, World!")
(def char-val (char s 0))
(def multi "Line 1
Line 2")
strings.notes: Racket represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Racket formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Racket, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: Racket constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.notes: Racket achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.notes: Racket emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in Racket are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Racket uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: Racket provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.notes: Racket isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
